title: Embedding dimension compatibility adapter and staged live reindex strategy
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Allow Redwood serving and client SDKs to handle heterogeneous embedding vector dimensionalities during a transition (dim increase or decrease) while minimizing downtime, avoiding large-scale reindex windows, and preserving reranking quality. This ticket implements a compatibility adapter in the serving runtime + SDK shims and defines a staged live reindex strategy for existing indexes.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes an 'embedding_schema_version' header for indexing/query APIs and accepts requests for legacy dims (e.g., 512) and target dims (e.g., 1024) concurrently without 5xx errors.
Serving adapter can transparently pad/truncate vectors for model-compatibility with deterministic semantics and documented accuracy implications.
Client SDK (Python/TS) includes opt-in adapter mode that negotiates schema version on init and falls back to safe shim if server supports mixed dims.
Live reindex workflow documented and automated (dry-run + canary + bulk), with an observable dashboard showing quality deltas and reindex progress.
End-to-end e2e test coverage added: synthetic queries show <5% drop in rerank NDCG during staggered rollout and restored baseline after full reindex.
Rollback path validated: index snapshot + config toggle to force single-dimension serving within 15 minutes.
Performance regression <10% tail latency at p95 compared to baseline under target traffic during canary phase.
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Ticket created after spike detection in rerank quality experiments for embedding dimension changes.
2026-03-07: Prototype adapter implemented in runtime: zero-copy pad to power-of-two dims and deterministic truncation for shrink paths. Initial microbench shows ~3% CPU overhead.
2026-03-08: SDK shim spec drafted; PM review requested. Discussed opt-in vs opt-out behavior with DX. Added negotiation header and explicit compatibility mode.

2026-03-09: Ran synthetic load with mixed-dimension reads against a single GPU node. Observed p95 increase at high-concurrency when adapter invokes memcpy; moved to continuous-batching path to amortize cost.
2026-03-10: Security reviewed padding semantics; no new data leakage. Prepared canary checklist and dashboard template. Assigned to release runtime-2.4.
2026-03-10: PM approved staged reindex plan pending A/B eval thresholds.
decisions: Prefer deterministic padding (append zeros) for dimension increases to preserve cosine similarity monotonicity; document expected quality artifacts.
For dimension shrink (target dim < stored dim) use deterministic truncation of trailing dimensions and provide optional PCA-based shrink tool as offline reindex alternative.
Adapter will run by default in server 'compat-mode' for 2 weeks in canary, then switched to opt-in in GA to force full reindex for customers who want absolute parity.
Keep index format versioned; do not mutate existing index files in-place during automatic compatibility mode to preserve rollback safety.
tradeoffs: Padding/truncation convenience vs small accuracy loss: zero-padding is cheap but can slightly bias similarity scores for some models.
On-the-fly adapter increases tail latency under high concurrency; mitigation requires batching/prefetch and prioritized KV cache warming.
Full reindex yields best quality but is operationally expensive; staged reindex reduces peak load but lengthens migration window.
benchmarks: Microbench: adapter zero-pad median extra CPU 2.8% under p50 throughput.
Load test (mixed dims 70/30): p95 latency +7% before batching optimization, +3% after batching path change.
Quality A/B: canary group (adapter) NDCG drop 3.7% vs fully reindexed baseline, improved to 1.1% after embedding-normalization patch.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Dry-run): feature flag off, collect metrics, run offline scoring to estimate quality impact (1 week).
Phase 1 (Canary): enable compat-mode on 10% of traffic for non-SLA customers; monitor p95/p99 latency, NDCG, cost per query (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (Staggered reindex): for customers with high quality delta, offer scheduled reindex windows using background bulk workers and quota throttles (4 weeks rolling).
Phase 3 (GA): SDK adds opt-out toggle; default is to require reindex for new schema but provide auto-compat for legacy customers for 30 days post-release.
Emergency rollback: toggle feature flag to force single-dim serving and route new writes to snapshot-backed index.
monitoring_and_alerts: Create dashboard panels: schema_version distribution, adapter_invocation_rate, avg_adapter_latency, ndcg_delta_by_customer, reindex_progress_by_index
Alerts: ndcg_delta > 8% for top-10 customers (critical), adapter p95 > 200ms (P1), reindex failure rate >1% (P1)
Audit logs for every on-the-fly transform (pad/truncate) with request id for post-mortem tracing
rollback_plan: Snapshot index and store in archived bucket before bulk reindex begins.
If quality regressions exceed thresholds, flip runtime compatibility flag to 'strict' which rejects mixed-dim queries and routes traffic to snapshot index version.
Provide script to backfill clients to old SDK behavior and a support runbook for manual reindex revert.

notes: This approach aims to reduce friction for customers during model upgrades that change embedding dimensionality while keeping a clear path to full-quality reindex. We must communicate accuracy tradeoffs and provide automated tooling for customers who require strict determinism.
final_comment: After canary and metrics validation, we'll prioritize building the offline PCA shrink tool for customers who cannot accept truncation artifacts. Track this as follow-up epic in Q2.
